run 16a5eee50cca, protected mode, blinded 0.1.0, 2.1.302 (Claude Code). train 2026-10-01T00:00:00, validation 2026-10-01T12:05:00, test 2026-10-01T18:05:00 to 2026-10-02T00:00:00.

1. Verdict

On the locked test window (18:05:00-00:00:00), arb strategy cvm_off47_tightwd on ATUSDT_MEXC hedged on ATUSDT_BINANCE, under the risk-averse queue model, the worse of the two, made +18.3 bps a fill net of a 10 bps hedge fee over 54 fills, +0.49 USD at a 5.12 USD size (90% CI +0.30 to +0.77 USD), at a Sharpe per sqrt-hour of +1.57; 2% picked off, drifting 30 USD of coin to ATUSDT_MEXC; the counterparty is one flow of 3,582 prints a day. It made no transfer between the venues on test.

Judged under rules v3.

Fee verdict: profitable at the brief's 10 bps taker fee; the 90% interval of net bps/hour on the score's blocks and draws is +3192.5 to +8086.9, and it stays above zero at a taker fee of 24.54 bps or lower (break-even 27.88 bps).

The fills are the strategy as written: a strategy built for a rebate would quote differently.

A feature below the dotted line did worse on validation than on train. Points drifting further below it as the run goes on is the overfitting the Ladder is there to limit.

Each strategy's validation Sharpe, which the agent never saw. A loop without a judge would ship the best so far; the Ladder releases one only when it clears the best by more than noise.

5 strategies were not released for holding positions too long for validation to judge. One hold is one bet however many blocks it spans, so a strategy's noise is measured in blocks as long as its time-weighted mean hold, and validation must hold 20 of them: gap_z_hold (trial 22), holds of 22 min, 15 in validation; mm_gap_lean (trial 24), holds of 5 h 51 min, 1 in validation; mm_gap_withdraw (trial 25), holds of 1 h 4 min, 5 in validation; band_breach_hold (trial 32), holds of 57 min, 6 in validation; gap_dev_two_leg (trial 33), holds of 2 h 21 min, 2 in validation.

3. Deflation

N = 23 distinct strategies over the whole run, error rows included (0 of them refused archetypes), across K = 2 edges: speed & information 8, liquidity & flow 15. Each edge has its own Ladder, so the run leaks up to K times the bits of one. Released: speed & information 1 feature and 0 strategies; liquidity & flow 1 feature and 2 strategies.

The chosen strategy's validation Sharpe is +2.56 per sqrt-hour. After 23 trials, of 2 edges, the expected maximum under the null is +3.03; the deflated Sharpe probability is 0.106.

After this many trials, a validation Sharpe of +2.56 is within what noise would produce.

Probability of backtest overfitting (CSCV): 0.03.

4. The signal

Shown on train, validation and test, by edge and then by archetype. Each archetype's pick is the rule of a families run kept to its own trials: the final strategy's, else the last released, else the best on validation. Test appears only when the final strategy was scored there.

cross_venue_arbitrage: Cross-venue arbitrage

Pairs: ATUSDT_MEXC over ATUSDT_BINANCE, gap_dev_two_leg (trial 33), the pairs strategy with the best validation Sharpe; it was not released

Fitted on the trailing 10m before each 10m clock window and held through it; bands at z 2 in and 0.5 out, from the brief's pairs defaults; the strategy's own could not be read.

The spread is the log mid of A less the hedge ratio times that of B, here less its walk-forward mean, in bps. Its level jumps at every refit, so the mean is taken off. The dashed lines are where the strategy goes in, the dotted ones where it comes out, and the shading is where it held the spread.

The hedge ratio, the units of B the spread holds against one of A, fitted on the window before each clock window. A ratio that wanders makes the B leg trade at every refit.

How fast the spread came back inside each clock window: the half-life of an AR(1) fit. An open circle is a window where it did not come back at all. The dashed line is what the same fit reads on a pure random walk in a window this long, since the fitted slope sits below 1 even with no reversion: only points well under it show the spread coming back.

In the markout fan of the spread, every time its z-score went past the entry band of ±2 counts as a trade back toward the mean: short the spread when z is high, long when it is low. Events are at least 70 s apart. The line is the average move of the spread in that direction, at the hedge ratio of the moment, with two standard errors either side. A spread that reverts rises after zero. Breaking even takes crossing the spread of both legs twice, the B leg scaled by the hedge ratio, and the fees of both on top.

The strategy: mm_gap_withdraw (trial 25), the accepted strategy with the best validation Sharpe; it was not released

Four fill models, each its own closed loop on the recorded book and trades: T fills only when a trade goes through the quote, RA joins the back of the displayed size and takes every cancel as behind it, PR takes cancels from ahead of it in proportion, and F is always at the front. Every number is in bps of one unit at the first mid of the segment. The judge scores the lower of RA's and PR's Sharpe in the score's column, each measured on blocks at least as long as that model's time-weighted mean hold, since one hold is one bet however many blocks it spans; the column before it is the same P&L on the brief's 5 min blocks.

After each fill: the mid's move in the fill's direction, weighted by units, for each model. A maker's fill sits below the mid at 0 by what it captured, and pays the fee; the line has to stay above the break-even for the fill to pay. Lines that fall after 0 are adverse selection.

How it dies. Adverse selection. You get filled most just before the price moves against you. Faster makers take the front of the queue, and a fee change can erase the margin.

The strategy: cvm_off47_tightwd (trial 36), the final strategy

Quoted on ATUSDT_MEXC and every fill hedged on ATUSDT_BINANCE as a taker at its depth as-of the hedge's arrival. Four fill models, each its own closed loop, with a trade through the quote filling no more than its print. Per fill, in bps of the fill at the hedge venue's mid: captured, the maker leg against that mid; delay, its move until the hedge arrived; slippage, the hedge against the mid then; fees, both legs'; net, their sum. Picked off is a fill whose price that mid had already passed; drift is the USD of coin a day moved onto the quote venue. The judge scores the lower of RA's and PR's Sharpe on net per block, both legs, each on blocks at least as long as its holds (the brief's 5 min).

cvm_off47_tightwd
import polars as pl
import blinded as bl

cv = bl.cross_venue_making(quote="ATUSDT_MEXC", hedge="ATUSDT_BINANCE")
FAIR = (pl.col("ATUSDT_BINANCE.bid"), pl.col("ATUSDT_BINANCE.ask"))


@cv.strategy(requires=["micro_gap_fast"])
def cvm_off55(panel, features):
    g = features["micro_gap_fast"]
    bid = pl.when(g < -25).then(None).otherwise(55)
    ask = pl.when(g > 25).then(None).otherwise(55)
    return bl.quote(bid=bid, ask=ask, size=32.0, max_inventory=320.0, fair=FAIR)


@cv.strategy(requires=["micro_gap_fast"])
def cvm_off47_big(panel, features):
    g = features["micro_gap_fast"]
    bid = pl.when(g < -25).then(None).otherwise(47)
    ask = pl.when(g > 25).then(None).otherwise(47)
    return bl.quote(bid=bid, ask=ask, size=64.0, max_inventory=640.0, fair=FAIR)


@cv.strategy(requires=["micro_gap_fast"])
def cvm_off47_tightwd(panel, features):
    g = features["micro_gap_fast"]
    bid = pl.when(g < -15).then(None).otherwise(47)
    ask = pl.when(g > 15).then(None).otherwise(47)
    return bl.quote(bid=bid, ask=ask, size=32.0, max_inventory=320.0, fair=FAIR)
micro_gap_fast
import blinded as bl
from blinded import features as F

mm = bl.market_making(instrument="ATUSDT_MEXC")
cv = bl.cross_venue_making(quote="ATUSDT_MEXC", hedge="ATUSDT_BINANCE")


def _gap():
    return (F.microprice("ATUSDT_BINANCE").log() - F.mid("ATUSDT_MEXC").log()) * 1e4


@mm.feature("Binance microprice gap to MEXC mid, ewm 1 s: the freshest stale-quote signal before MEXC reprices")
def micro_gap_fast(panel):
    return F.ewm_mean(_gap(), 10)


@mm.feature("Binance microprice gap to MEXC mid clipped at +-40 bps then smoothed 3 s: outlier gaps are Binance thin-book noise")
def micro_gap_clipped(panel):
    g = _gap().clip(-40.0, 40.0)
    return F.ewm_mean(g, 30)


@cv.feature("Binance micro gap to MEXC mid, plus MEXC own top-of-book imbalance in half-spreads: both say where MEXC reprices")
def micro_gap_plus_mexc_imb(panel):
    g = F.ewm_mean(_gap(), 30)
    hs = F.spread("ATUSDT_MEXC") / F.mid("ATUSDT_MEXC") * 1e4 / 2.0
    imb = F.ewm_mean(F.imbalance("ATUSDT_MEXC"), 50)
    return g + (imb * hs).fill_null(0.0)

NOTES.md
# NOTES
- Primary horizon 10s; MEXC spread ~120bps, mid moves ~1/s, so slow gap-closing features work best.
- S1 speed&info: binance_mexc_gap_dev (trial 1, lead_lag; log Binance-MEXC mid gap less trailing 10min mean) train rankIC 0.12@10s, RELEASED (best 0.15).
- mexc_imb_smooth (trial 2, OBI, ewm 5s of top imbalance): train rankIC ~0.045, not released.
- theo_minus_mexc (trial 3, arb, theo vs MEXC mid net basis): train rankIC ~0.046, not released.
- IC grows with horizon (60s 0.23) for the gap feature; try longer-memory/different demeaning, depth imbalance (Binance depth), trade flow next.
- Bash: write files with Write tool; no shell loops.
- S2 liquidity&flow: binance_micro_vs_mexc_mid (trial 4, MM; Binance microprice vs MEXC mid, ewm 3s) train rankIC 0.19@10s, RELEASED (best 0.15). binance_flow_30s (5, MM, trade imbalance) 0.03@10s, not released. gap_vs_hour_median (6, CVM, gap less 1h median) 0.156@10s, not released.
- Gap-type features (Binance level vs MEXC mid) dominate; flow features weak. Next: MEXC spread/queue-based features, theo sd/innovation, depth_imbalance of Binance (5 levels).
- S3 speed: binance_lead_gap_30s (8, lead_lag; Binance 30s return less MEXC's) rankIC 0.008@10s, not released (raw IC 0.12 but rank low). binance_depth_imb (9, OBI; own 5-level Binance imbalance, ewm 5s) rankIC 0.046@10s, not released. F.depth_imbalance raises ZeroDivisionError on empty levels: write own with guard (import polars OK).
- Return-based leads are weak; level gaps (Binance vs MEXC mid) remain the only winners. Untried: MEXC spread/staleness-conditioned gap, theo sd/innovation_z.
- S4 liquidity: micro_gap_demeaned (10, MM; ewm3s micro gap less 10min mean) rankIC 0.13@10s; micro_gap_slow (11, MM, ewm 20s) 0.187@10s; theo_vs_mexc_bps (12, CVM) 0.12@10s. None released (best 0.15; trial 4 is 0.19 train). Smoothing/demeaning variants of the micro gap don't add; submit takes >2 min (runs in background, wait with until-loop). Next: MEXC spread/staleness-conditioned features, not more gap variants.
- S5 speed: binance_in_mexc_band (13, lead_lag; Binance-MEXC mid gap in MEXC half-spreads, demeaned 10min) 0.11@10s, not released (same as gap_dev; spread-normalising adds nothing). mexc_flow_persist (14, trade_flow_persistence; MEXC 5min trade imbalance) ~0 IC (-0.03@10s): MEXC trade flow is useless (1 trade/30s). Gap-level family is exhausted; flow/imbalance dead. Little left for speed edge.
- S6 liquidity: micro_gap_fast (15, MM, ewm 1s) 0.197@10s, micro_gap_clipped (16, MM, clip ±40bps) 0.194 (identical to trial 4: clipping no-op), micro_gap_plus_mexc_imb (17, CVM, + MEXC imbalance*half-spread) 0.143 (worse: MEXC imbalance adds noise). None released (best 0.15; judged on val, trial 4 only one released). Micro-gap family exhausted; no further liquidity features worth trying -> phase_done.
- S7 speed: gap_zscore (18, lead_lag; gap z-scored by trailing 10min mean/sd) 60s rankIC 0.237, not released (best 0.15). Another gap variant; no new info. Speed edge exhausted -> phase_done.
- S8 liquidity: mexc_mid_reversion (19, MM, MEXC mid vs own 60s ewm) ~0 IC (-0.02@10s); micro_gap_over_hedge_spread (20, CVM, micro gap / Binance spread) 0.17@10s, not released. Nothing beats trial 4. Family exhausted -> phase_done.
- S9 speed STRATEGIES: taker threshold strategies on lead_lag gap features all lose (trial 21 gap_dev_rare SR -1.9, 22 gap_z_hold -1.34, 23 micro_gap_rare -1.26; none released). Crossing MEXC's ~120bps spread (+8bps fee) swamps a ~10-50bps gap signal; gross/fill ~ -48bps. Only a maker-style (quote) strategy can work (maker proxy was positive: +61bps/fill) -> belongs to liquidity edge, not speed taker. Don't retry taker thresholds with other gap features.
- S10 liquidity STRATEGIES (strategies/liq_strats.py; use pl.col("ATUSDT_BINANCE.bid") for fair, F has no bid/ask): cvm_off_binance (26, CVM; quote 47 ticks (~30bps) off Binance touch, side withdrawn when micro_gap_fast beyond ±25bps, size 32) train SR 1.06, 54 fills, 0% picked off, RELEASED (best 2). mm_gap_lean (24, MM; join touch, lean=0.5*gap ticks) SR 0.65 but only 24 fills (lumpy, inventory-driven), not released. mm_gap_withdraw (25, MM; join touch, withdraw side on ±25bps gap) SR 0.40, 3 fills, not released. MM fills are very rare (few trades on MEXC): CVM is the better vehicle. Next: CVM offset sweep (35-45 ticks for more fills), larger size, theo as fair.
- S11 liquidity STRATEGIES (strategies/cvm_sweep.py): cvm_off38 (30, CVM, 38 ticks off Binance, same gap withdraw) train SR ~1.0, net 2296 bps/h; cvm_gap_skew (31, CVM, offsets 42∓0.5*gap ticks clipped 25-70) SR 1.07, 1945 bps/h; ~60 fills each. Neither released (best 2; trial 26 at 47 ticks is still SR 1.06 / 2702 bps/h). Closer offsets and gap-skew don't beat the plain 47-tick quote; fills stay ~60 and are the limit. Untried: size/max_inventory increase, theo as fair, wider offset (55+) for fewer picked-off.
- S12 speed STRATEGIES: band_breach_hold (32, lead_lag; binance_in_mexc_band z>3.5, exit 0) SR -0.58; gap_dev_two_leg (33, arb; gap_dev z>4 long MEXC/short Binance) SR -0.57; ~12 fills, gross -21bps/fill. Neither released. Taker strategies on the speed edge are structurally negative (120bps MEXC spread, no visible cross); stop trying them -> phase_done.
- S13 liquidity STRATEGIES (strategies/cvm_s13.py): cvm_off55 (34, 55 ticks) SR 0.98 not released; cvm_off47_big (35, size 64/inv 640) SR 1.03 identical to 26 (size doesn't change SR), not released; cvm_off47_tightwd (36, withdraw at ±15bps instead of 25) SR 1.06, RELEASED (best 2.6). Tighter withdrawal helps a little; untried: withdraw ±10, theo as fair.
- S14 liquidity STRATEGIES (strategies/cvm_s14.py): cvm_off47_wd8 (37, withdraw ±8) SR 0.94; cvm_theo_fair (38, theo as fair, wd 15) SR 0.93; cvm_two_speed_wd (39, fast±15 or slow±10 withdraw) SR 1.01. None released (best 2.6). Tighter than ±15 hurts; theo fair worse than Binance touch. CVM 47-tick family is saturated at SR ~1 on train (~50 fills); stop.
- S15 liquidity STRATEGIES (strategies/cvm_s15.py): cvm_off47_invskew (40, skew 0.1) SR 1.07, 3088 bps/h; cvm_favour_tight (41, 40 ticks on favourable side) SR 1.11, 2561 bps/h. Neither released (best 2.6). Still ~60 fills, SR ~1 ceiling; inventory skew and side-tilt add nothing. CVM exhausted -> phase_done.
- S16 liquidity STRATEGIES (strategies/cvm_s16.py): cvm_wide_when_thin (offset 60 when Binance spread>10bps) SR 1.04; cvm_pause_thin (no quotes when Binance spread>12bps) SR 0.96. Neither released (best 2.6). Hedge-spread conditioning adds nothing; SR ~1 ceiling holds. CVM exhausted -> phase_done.

# DATA: tardis-arb-atusdt-mexc-binance-2026-10-01

File `train.parquet`, sha256 `2dfa5addd51be023`.
Clock: receive. Grid: 100ms steps, 431,985 points, 2026-10-01 00:00:00+00:00 to 2026-10-01 11:59:58.400000+00:00; warm-up 5min.

Scoring windows (warm-up removed):
- train [2026-10-01T00:05:00+00:00, 2026-10-01T12:00:00+00:00)
- val [2026-10-01T12:05:00+00:00, 2026-10-01T18:00:00+00:00)
- test [2026-10-01T18:05:00+00:00, 2026-10-02T00:00:00+00:00)

## Streams

Gaps are between distinct timestamps; `stale_share` is the share of grid points whose latest event is older than one grid step.

| stream | instrument | rows | duplicate_rows | events_per_s | median_gap_ms | p90_gap_ms | stale_share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| book | ATUSDT_BINANCE | 11,281 | 2,579 | 0.2014 | 1.976 | 1.197e+04 | 0.9932 |
| book | ATUSDT_MEXC | 11,553 | 0 | 0.2674 | 1292 | 9000 | 0.9752 |
| theo | THEO.ATUSDT | 22,834 | 2,579 | 0.4689 | 221.7 | 6159 | 0.9697 |
| trades | ATUSDT_BINANCE | 1,537 | 481 | 0.02445 | 774 | 1.261e+05 | 0.9986 |
| trades | ATUSDT_MEXC | 1,579 | 37 | 0.0357 | 2.25e+04 | 5.304e+04 | 0.9965 |

## Cross-stream lag

Lag that maximises the correlation of 100 ms log returns over +-500 ms, searched in 10 ms then 1 ms steps. Positive: the first stream moves first. A peak correlation under 0.1 is not a clear peak and its lag is noise.

| first | second | lag_ms | corr_at_lag | corr_at_0 | clear_peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| book ATUSDT_BINANCE | trades ATUSDT_BINANCE | -1 | 0.4851 | 0.4851 | yes |
| book ATUSDT_MEXC | trades ATUSDT_MEXC | 8 | 0.1056 | 0.1056 | yes |
| book ATUSDT_BINANCE | book ATUSDT_MEXC | 32 | 0.213 | 0.1692 | yes |

## Trade stamps against the book

Share of trades printed at the touch (buy at the ask, sell at the bid) when the book is read just before trade time + offset, offsets -200 to +20 ms in 1 ms steps. A peak at a negative offset means trades are stamped late relative to the book.

| instrument | best_offset_ms | share_at_best | share_at_0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ATUSDT_BINANCE | -1 | 0.7625 | 0.5823 |
| ATUSDT_MEXC | 1 | 0.02407 | 0.0228 |

## The touch stream

The fill engine reads every top-of-book row of ATUSDT_MEXC from the touch file `train.touch.parquet` (11,553 rows here), in ticks of 1e-05, and each trade at its own stamp; features never see it. Over this workspace's rows:

| measure | value |
|---|---|
| mid, median; tick | 0.155235; 1e-05 = 0.644 bps |
| spread one tick wide, share of time; two ticks | 0.00%; 0.00% |
| book rows (a second); distinct stamps | 11,553 (0); 11,553 |
| trades (a second) | 1,579 (0.0) |
| displayed at the touch, median bid; ask; bid in USD | 571.2; 536; 89 |
| falls of the best bid; traded out; pulled; partly | 641; 0.3%; 99.7%; 0.0% |
| median time between changes of the best bid price | 1,890 ms |
| rows at an unchanged bid price; of them with the bid's size changed | 8,551; 371 |

A fall of the best bid is traded out when the sells at the old price from 100 ms before its last row to the fall reach the size it showed, pulled when there were none, and partly each otherwise. Where most levels are traded out, a quote at the back of the touch fills when the level is swept; where many are pulled, the two queue models disagree most.

## The venues on this file

Every book row of each venue is on the one receive clock; `age_ms` is how long after the exchange's stamp the recorder received it, none where the venue sends no stamp. Over this workspace's rows:

| | ATUSDT_BINANCE | ATUSDT_MEXC |
|---|---|---|
| mid, time-weighted median; tick in bps | 0.1554; none | 0.1555; 0.64 |

## Who prints on each venue

A flow of near-uniform sizes at a regular pace, printing at prices nobody showed as the touch, is one counterparty, not a market: a quote that fills against it fills against that one process, which may change when the quote is there.

## The depth file

`train.depth.parquet` holds ATUSDT_BINANCE's book to 25 levels a side at every snapshot (10,431 rows here), read only by the hedge leg as-of its arrival; its level 0 trails the touch stream by about 100 ms. Over this workspace's rows:

ATUSDT_BINANCE: 11,281 touch rows and 10,431 snapshot rows. The snapshot's level 0 as-of each touch row's stamp plus a lag shows the touch's prices and sizes on 40.9% and 1.2% at 0 ms, 43.4% and 5.1% at 10 ms, 62.4% and 27.0% at 100 ms; the touch as-of each snapshot row shows its level 0 prices on 99.9% and sizes on 99.7% of them (the build refuses under 90%); 25.4% of touch rows cross the as-of snapshot's level 0.

## Venues

ATUSDT_MEXC and ATUSDT_BINANCE are one product on two venues. Venue feed cadence: ATUSDT_BINANCE's book, median gap 1.976 ms between distinct receive stamps; the largest 10 ms bin, 20 to 30 ms, holds 1% of gaps. A lead of the other venue shorter than this cannot be told from the schedule; D11 of the report repeats it on each segment. On the receive clock a lead of one venue over the other can be market lead or feed path.

## Lead-lag on train

C(tau) is the correlation of the leader's last 100 ms log return at each grid point with the follower's 100 ms return ending tau later, over whole steps from -10 to +10 and 10 ms steps across one step either side. A follower that copies with a delay peaks at that delay. `c_after_fill` is C on the follower's first whole step after a taker's fill (50 ms after the decision, so tau = 150 ms), the step a taker holds; `best_after_fill` the largest C from there on; `usable_by_taker` says yes when that is positive and at least half the peak, a rule of thumb.

| leader | follower | lag_at_peak_ms | c_at_peak | c_after_fill | best_after_fill | usable_by_taker |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ATUSDT_MEXC | ATUSDT_BINANCE | -20 | 0.2084 | -0.002106 | 0.002919 | no |
| ATUSDT_BINANCE | ATUSDT_MEXC | 30 | 0.2115 | -0.00278 | 0.01903 | no |

## Pairs on train

Each pair A over B fitted as `bl.pairs` fits it at the brief's defaults: OLS of ln m_A on ln m_B over the trailing 2h, refitted at each 30m clock window. `hedge_ratio` and `residual_sd_bps` are the fit in force at the end of train; `median_half_life_s` is the AR(1) half-life of the spread in each clock window, the median over windows (none when most did not revert), and `no_reversion` the share of windows where it did not come back at all. A pairs feature is scored against the spread return at equal notional, A's forward log return less B's.

| pair | hedge_ratio | residual_sd_bps | median_half_life_s | no_reversion | windows |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ATUSDT_MEXC over ATUSDT_BINANCE | 1.141 | 13.3 | 42.31 | 0 | 23 |

## Caveats

- Rows with identical timestamps resolve by file order, last wins.
- Which instruments are in the file, and why, is for the user to own.
- Receive clock: a lead of one stream over another can be market lead or feed delay; these numbers cannot tell them apart.

## The raw files behind tardis-arb-atusdt-mexc-binance-2026-10-01.parquet

Built by `blinded demo arb` from the Tardis free day 2026-10-01: ATUSDT spot on `mexc` (instrument ATUSDT_MEXC, the quote venue) and `binance` (ATUSDT_BINANCE, the hedge venue), `book_ticker`, `trades` and `book_snapshot_25` of each, every stamp Tardis's `local_timestamp`, the recorder's receive clock. Tardis files have no checksum; their sizes and SHA-256 are these:

| file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---|
| mexc_book_ticker_2026-10-01_ATUSDT.csv.gz | 645,227 | `a6b7c76609dd6f3c` |
| mexc_trades_2026-10-01_ATUSDT.csv.gz | 86,382 | `cd299eed232ecbda` |
| mexc_book_snapshot_25_2026-10-01_ATUSDT.csv.gz | 5,446,963 | `2c67cd8f07c8e1fc` |

| binance_book_snapshot_25_2026-10-01_ATUSDT.csv.gz | 1,730,685 | `d636d533d36378b9` |

The data file keeps every book row of both venues, with `age_ms`, how long after the exchange's stamp the recorder received the row (0 where the venue sends none), the hedge venue's levels 1 to 4 from its snapshot as-of each of its rows, and every trade with its own venue's touch as received. Nothing is thinned: the quote venue changes its touch about once a second, and the hedge leg reads the hedge venue's touch at fill stamps that are on no lattice. The touch file `tardis-arb-atusdt-mexc-binance-2026-10-01.touch.parquet` holds every two-sided row of ATUSDT_MEXC in ticks of 1e-05; the depth file `tardis-arb-atusdt-mexc-binance-2026-10-01.depth.parquet` every snapshot row of ATUSDT_BINANCE, 25 levels a side in price units. Only the sims read the two. Ticks: ATUSDT_MEXC 1e-05, ATUSDT_BINANCE 0.0001; lot 1.0 on the quote venue. Fees in the brief: maker 0 and taker 8 bps on the quote venue (its exchangeInfo), the hedge 10 bps (Binance's regular spot tier); the stock block's `withdrawal_fee_coin` is unset: look it up on both venues' withdrawal pages before an arbitrage strategy is scored.

The quote venue's spread on the other free days in the raw directory, time-weighted median: 2026-09-01: 112.0 bps; 2026-08-01: 11.3 bps; 2026-07-01: 8.0 bps. A wide day is a month with no maker on the quote venue; the build refuses a day under three hedge fees.


## The theo

`F.theo("ATUSDT")` is a Kalman filter's consolidated price of ATUSDT over ATUSDT_MEXC, ATUSDT_BINANCE: one latent log price and one basis per venue, each quote a reading of the two with its own noise; the anchor (ATUSDT_BINANCE 1) fixes the origin, so the theo is quoted in the anchor's terms. It was computed once at init, causally, one event at a time, and is a column of the panel (`THEO.ATUSDT.theo`, `.sd_bps`, `.innovation_z`, `.basis_<venue>`).

Fitted on train only, by the prediction-error likelihood on its stream conflated to one event per venue per second (10,178 events, 201 evaluations, negative log likelihood -67,642.2): price volatility 1.72 bps per sqrt-second, quote noise ATUSDT_MEXC 1.4, ATUSDT_BINANCE 7.71 bps, event-clock weight 0.316; the basis wander held at 0.02 bps per sqrt-second, not fitted.

| segment | venue | events | z mean | z variance | z lag-1 autocorrelation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| train | ATUSDT_MEXC | 11,553 | -0.039 | 1.234 | 0.354 |
| train | ATUSDT_BINANCE | 11,281 | +0.066 | 0.773 | 0.920 |

A filter that fits gives z of mean 0, variance 1 and no autocorrelation; validation and test are filtered with train's parameters, so a regime change shows there as innovations that stop being white.
